findings.title: Both halves of the "must EQUAL, not merely appear in" confirmation are unpinned: degrading either exact-ref equality to substring containment survives all 84 tests
findings.reason: The docblock, MINT_ADMIN_USAGE and docs/runbooks/mint-admin.md all promise that --confirm-ref must EQUAL the ref parsed out of BOTH halves of the target, 'not merely appear in it'. Once --env production lifts the denylist, those two equalities are the ONLY controls left between a typed selector and a production write. Mutants S8 (Supabase half) and S9 (database half) each replace the equality with substring containment and each survives the individual test and a full 84-test run. Fix: add a superstring case per half that only equality can refuse — supabaseUrl 'https://xx' + STAGING_REF + '.supabase.co' with confirmRef STAGING_REF, and dbTarget 'postgres@' + STAGING_REF + '-shadow.example.com:5432' with dbProjectRef '(ref-not-found)' — and assert the discriminating message /resolves to project ref .*, not the confirmed/ instead of /supabase/i and /database/i. Each addition kills its mutant.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutation-derived, both confirmed non-equivalent and both on branches the named tests execute. S8: refFromSupabaseUrl requires the first host label to be exactly /^[a-z0-9]{20}$/ AND equal to the confirmation; containment additionally accepts a 22-character label and a ref appearing anywhere in the URL path or query. S9: the mutant never reads dbProjectRef at all, so the documented sentinel guarantee ((ref-not-found)/(unparseable) can never confirm) is destroyed while the sentinel test still passes on fixture luck. Neither is an equivalent mutation and neither is unexecuted, so these are claims about the MUTANT surviving a real oracle — survived-confirmed-P0, not inconclusive.

findings.title: main()'s `allowProduction: args.envMode === 'production'` — the only wiring between the operator's selector and the guard — has no covering test at any level
findings.reason: Both ends of the join are pinned (the guard by six killed mutants S1-S6; the parse default by A1) but the join itself is executed by nothing. A mutant `allowProduction: true` would let ambient, local and staging reach a production project with a matching --confirm-ref and would ship green. Fix: extract the guard-input assembly (e.g. `export function buildMintGuardInput(args, config): MintTargetInput`) and assert allowProduction is true for 'production' and false for each of 'ambient', 'local', 'staging' — a four-row it.each.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not mutation-derived: Step 2 Direction B classifies a production hunk with no identified covering candidate as P1 (uncovered change) with an inconclusive/oracle inventory row. Established by reverse import search — `rg -l mint-admin` returns only the module and its three suites, `main` is not exported, and the unit suite's own header records that importing the module runs nothing because runDirectCli fires only on direct Node invocation.
